About

Hello! I am a Junior at Penn studying Computer Science and Mathematics. I am also pursuing an Accelerated Masters in Robotics from the GRASP Lab. My current interests are

  • Deep Learning
  • Applied Optimization
  • Controls for Robotics

Recently, I have been working on finding better optimization methods for multi-task representation learning with Thomas Zhang – who wrote a wonderful writeup of the project here – among others.

I am currently on the search for engineering and research internships related to robotics or machine learning for the summer of 2025. If you are interested in learning more about my experience feel free to scroll through my projects below.

Outside of work, I play soccer, DJ for events around campus and am involved with Penn Student Government. Contact me at farazr [at] seas [dot] upenn [dot] edu.

Projects

Optimizing for Representation Learning

This project explores algorithms that split model training into two parts: learning representations (i.e. Phi) and learning task heads (i.e. F^(t)). The work is motivated by the fact that classical methods don't work well in this setting. Tap here to see a one page description written by the lead of this project Thomas Zhang.

SwiftScore

SwiftScore is the world's first Assignment Management Platform - a SaaS tool that aims to save teachers time using AI-assisted grading, analytics, and remediation tools all in one. I worked on early engineering for the platform, particularly on integrating our services with Google Classroom. I am still involved with the company, although I am now focused on product and strategy.

Decision Making Diffusion Models

Thinking of DDPMS as a stochastic process, we explore how different time intervals in the diffusion trajectory affect the features/structure that show up in the final sample. More importantly, I learned to train large models on (multiple) GPUs, got my toes wet with generative modeling theory, and made a lot of cool friends while working on this project in Prof. Eric Wong's Brachio Lab under Anton Xue during my Sophomore summer.

Click to learn more

TyPorch - C++ ML Compiler

TyPorch began as means for me to learn how ML works beyond model.fit() after my freshman Big Data course, but unintentionally became my first interaction with optimization algorithms, high performance (parallel) computing, C++, and shaped many of my interests throughout the rest of my time at Penn. I was able to train moderately sized (10k parameter) feedforward models on toy data, but never finished working all the way through benchmarking on the MNIST dataset.
